idiom_name: Vec<T> via sqlx query_as/#[derive(FromRow)] (or rusqlite query_map)
implementation_notes: Rust has no rowset type and does not want one: the record set is a Vec of typed structs produced by a mapping layer. sqlx::query_as prepares, executes and builds each row into the output type through the FromRow trait (implemented for tuples up to 16 elements; #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] generates it for structs), so query_as::<_, OrderRow>(...).fetch_all(&pool).await yields Result<Vec<OrderRow>>; rusqlite does the same by hand with prepare(...).query_map(params, |row| Ok(OrderRow { id: row.get(0)?, email: row.get(1)? }))? collected into a Vec. What replaces the classic structure is the struct plus the collection; generic dynamic rows (sqlx::Row::try_get with runtime column names, Vec<HashMap<String, Value>>) exist but trade away compiler checks - use them only when the column names genuinely are data.
pitfalls: sqlx's Row borrows from the connection's row buffer: a value must be copied into owned types before the next row is fetched - keeping Row values across iterations does not compile, and raw pointers into the buffer would go stale.

Nullability must be modelled exactly: a nullable column needs Option<T>, and a width mismatch (i32 vs i64) fails at runtime with a decoding error unless the compile-time-checked query macros are used.
Field-to-column binding is by name for derived structs (position for tuples): a changed column alias silently fails to bind, and #[sqlx(rename)] is required when the SQL name differs.
